Recent indicators suggest that activity has been expanding at a solid pace, but the decision to hold the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continue balance-sheet runoff aligns with New-Keynesian policy guidance (Clarida, Galí, Gertler) and Taylor-rule style responses to inflation above target. The emphasis on policy lags and vigilance toward inflation risks reflects the credibility considerations highlighted by Barro–Gordon and the importance of central bank independence in anchoring expectations (Bernanke). The reference to tighter credit conditions is consistent with the financial accelerator mechanism (Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist), implying downside risk to growth even as the banking system is described as sound. Ongoing QT in Treasuries and agency MBS should also keep broader financial conditions firm via term-premium channels (Cochrane–Piazzesi). Overall tone is mildly hawkish: growth-positive, inflation-wary, and data-dependent.
